query: tobacco retail licence density within 800 metres of secondary schools current smoking vaping students state licensing list 2025 school health survey
sourcesConsulted: general knowledge of the tobacco control literature
gradeRationale: Consistent associations between retailer density and youth smoking have been reported across several countries.
synthesis: The recorded search returned no records, so these five items are leads from general knowledge, not retrieved records. They suggest that more retailers near schools go with more student smoking, that the association weakens after adjustment for deprivation, and that caps reduce outlet numbers slowly.

items.title: Retailer density near schools and adolescent smoking: a multilevel analysis of a national school survey
items.keyFindings: Students at schools with five or more retailers within 800 metres had higher odds of current smoking (odds ratio 1.35) than students at schools with none, after adjustment for school deprivation.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; not retrieved.

items.title: Tobacco retail licensing and outlet density: a systematic review of effects on youth smoking
items.authors: Marchetti-Oyewole D, Sandoval-Kerr J, Tanaka-Bright E
items.keyFindings: Most of 19 studies found higher youth smoking with greater outlet density near schools or homes, but effects shrank with better adjustment for area deprivation.

items.title: Vape shops, convenience stores and student vaping: a spatial analysis
items.keyFindings: Vaping was more common among students at schools near specialist vape shops than near convenience stores only.
items.limitations: Not peer reviewed; year not known.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; no year or quality rating available.

items.title: Density near home or near school? Exposure windows for adolescent tobacco retail
items.keyFindings: Density around the home was associated with smoking as strongly as density around the school.
items.limitations: Home address available for a subsample only.

items.title: Licence caps near schools after five years: changes in outlet counts and youth smoking
items.keyFindings: Caps reduced outlet numbers near schools gradually; changes in youth smoking could not be attributed to them.

summary: Five leads recalled after an empty search, with a certainty label.
